citation.authors: Halegoua-DeMarzio D, Navarro V, Ahmad J, Avula B et al

record.population: Ten people in the US Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network with turmeric-associated liver injury (eight women; nine White; median age 56)
record.design: Case series with chemical analysis of products and HLA genetic typing
record.finding: Five were hospitalised and one died of acute liver failure. Injury began 1 to 4 months after starting, mostly hepatocellular, and turmeric was confirmed in all seven products tested (three also contained black pepper extract). Seven carried HLA-B*35:01 (allele frequency 0.45 against 0.06 to 0.07 in controls). The authors say turmeric liver injury appears to be increasing.
record.note: A small case series, mostly White participants, so it says nothing about how common the HLA type is in other populations. HLA-B*35:01 is the measured variable.
